operator: Amazon Web Services (Amazon Data Services, Inc.)
load_basis: Epoch AI estimate of IT power at 23 Dec 2025 (Buildings 1-11 operational), derived from satellite imagery and air permits, not an Amazon or utility figure. Year-end capacity, not a 2025 average: Epoch puts the site at 398 MW IT from about June 2025 (Buildings 1-7) until Buildings 8-11 came on in late December.
notes: Address 55001 Larrison Blvd, New Carlisle, IN 46552, St. Joseph County, per IDEM Part 70 permit T141-47750-00642 issued 28 Jan 2025 (https://permits.air.idem.in.gov/47750f.pdf), which authorizes 234 critical emergency generators of 2,750 kW each (643.5 MW nameplate). Coordinates are an OSM building footprint in the Larrison Blvd building cluster. Known fids osm:way/1303947602, osm:way/1471517731, /1471517732, /1471517734, /1471517735 and /1471517736 are footprints of this same campus and should not be counted separately. Utility: The Times (via GovTech, 23 Apr 2025) reports I&M will serve the site and that Amazon's IURC filings describe 2,250 MW at a 90% load factor; the tariff or contract form was not confirmed here, so arrangement is left unknown. Citizens Action Coalition's tracker (https://www.citact.org/data-centers) associates a 2,400 MW NIPSCO GenCo contract (IURC Cause No. 46322) with Amazon; that appears to concern Amazon's later Northwest Indiana sites and was not verified as serving this campus. Energized year: Epoch estimates Buildings 1-7 operational by 23 Jun 2025 from imagery; Amazon announced Project Rainier online in Oct 2025. No source found for any 2024 operation. Planned figure is contracted utility capacity (2,250 MW); Epoch projects 1,925 MW IT by 2028 and cites a 2.3 GW facility figure from the Buildings 19-32 air permit. Our inventory's 1,037 MW is Epoch's Oct 2026 value, not a 2025 value.

Confirms bi:611-0 is a real AWS data center, not a mislocated New Carlisle record: Inside INdiana Business (20 Dec 2023) reports Amazon building an $87M data center ($35M building, $52M IT equipment) in the AmeriPlex at the Port business park, Portage, with no opening timeline given. No street address found, so lat/lon left null; keep the known fid's coordinates. Utility is an inference from NIPSCO's service territory, not a sourced finding. Energized year not sourced: a Lakeshore Public Media article of 25 Nov 2025 surfaced in search results as saying AWS operates a smaller facility at AmeriPlex at the Port, but the page returned 404 on fetch and could not be read. Load not sourced. Our inventory's 65.2 MW is backup-generator nameplate; a $52M IT-equipment investment suggests the operating load is well below that (my inference, not a finding).

Google announced on 11 Dec 2025 that the facility was operational after about 18 months of construction (ground broken Apr 2024); campus of about 900 acres near East Tillman Road and Adams Center Road on Fort Wayne's southeast side. No street address found, so lat/lon left null; keep the known fid's coordinates. No MW figure published for the first building. Epoch AI (https://epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers/directory/google-fort-wayne) judges Building 1 not to be AI compute, lists 0 MW of AI IT power through 2026, and projects Building 2 operational about Dec 2026 (173 MW IT) rising to 863 MW IT by mid-2028 (about 1 GW facility power); the planned figure here is that IT projection, not a Google or utility number. Effective 2025 load is at most a few weeks of one building. Utility: Citizens Action Coalition's tracker lists the site under I&M (IURC Cause No. 46301); a Google-I&M demand response contract filed with the IURC in Aug 2025 appeared in search results but was not read directly, so arrangement is left unknown.

site_name: Meta Jeffersonville data center (River Ridge Commerce Center)
load_basis: Not operating at end of 2025. Epoch AI's imagery review found Buildings 1 and 2 shells and cooling complete but still under construction on 6 Mar 2026 and operational by 4 Jun 2026; Meta's Jan 2024 announcement expected operation in 2026.
notes: Not an end-of-2025 load; included to correct two known records. bi:609-0 (Meta, 9.0 MW, start 2025, at 38.3748, -85.6686 inside River Ridge Commerce Center) is the same campus as this fid and is a duplicate: its 2025 start year reflects a generator permit, not operation, and its coordinates look like the true site, while the epoch fid's coordinates fall in central Jeffersonville. No street address found, so lat/lon left null here. Utility: River Ridge's announcement names Duke Energy as a partner in enabling the investment, and Citizens Action Coalition's tracker describes the Clark County Meta site as the one large data center in Duke Energy Indiana territory (network upgrades in Cause No. 45647 TDSIC); the service arrangement is not stated. Planned figure is Epoch's 178 MW IT estimate for the nearly 700,000 sq ft, two-building campus, not a Meta or utility number.

site_name: Digital Crossroad (DX-1), former State Line Generating Plant
load_basis: Built capacity, an upper bound on operating load: The Times (via GovTech, 1 May 2025) reports a 105,000 sq ft building with 20 MW capacity, quotes developer testimony that the site can support only up to 20 MW via a dedicated substation, and says it reached capacity by early 2024.
notes: New site, not in known_facilities. Coordinates are the OSM building tagged Digital Crossroad on Digital Crossroad Drive, Hammond. Initial construction finished Nov 2020 per The Times; exact first-customer date not found, hence medium year confidence. Power is supplied by NIPSCO through a dedicated substation; tariff or contract form not stated. Planned figure is the existing 20 MW plus the 'over 200 MW' the developer is seeking for a roughly $7B expansion (DX3), which was not built in 2025; search results indicate a new NIPSCO subsidiary was approved to supply that expansion, not verified here.

serving_utility: WIN Energy REMC (wholesale supplier Hoosier Energy)
notes: New site, not in known_facilities, and the largest unresolved item for this state. Inside INdiana Business (11 May 2022) reports a five-year agreement to buy 115 MW from WIN Energy REMC for a mine on a 10-acre site adjacent to the Merom Generating Station, expected online within about 30 days, with the ability to cut load at regional peaks. Earthjustice (23 Oct 2023) describes it as opened in 2022, operating, and possibly the largest electricity user in the Hoosier Energy service area. Coordinates are the OSM centroid of the Merom power station, used as a proxy for the adjacent site, so approximate. 115 MW is a contracted maximum, not a measured load; no source gives actual operating MW, and 2025 status was not confirmed (a search result attributed to a Dec 2023 report says the CEO called the 2022 announcement outdated; not read directly, and the five-year term would run to about 2027). load_mw_2025 left null. If the mine ran near contract level in 2024 it alone would be on the order of EPRI's 94 average MW for the state.

site_name: DataBank Indianapolis IND2 and IND1 (Henry Street)
load_basis: Operator-published critical IT load: IND2 at 650 West Henry Street 3.75 MW plus IND1 at 731 West Henry Street 2.1 MW. Built capacity, an upper bound on operating load.
notes: Below the 10 MW threshold; included only to correct a known record. bi:608-0 sits at 650 West Henry Street (IND2; address from DataBank, geocoded with OSM Nominatim), about 150 m from IND1. Our inventory carries 19.7 MW for it, which is backup-generator nameplate and about three times the published critical IT load for both buildings combined. Opening year not sourced; our 2020 is a permit date. Utility is an inference from AES Indiana's Indianapolis service territory, not a sourced finding.
